Lesson title: What AI can and cannot do in Meta advertising
Objective: Explain which parts of campaign work AI speeds up and which decisions stay with you.
Demonstration: Slides with one side by side example of a raw AI draft and a human edited version of the same ad
Assignment: Write your business in four lines: what you sell, price in Naira, who buys, and how a customer pays you today.
Resources: Slide deck; Campaign file template (Campaign Planning Worksheet)

Lesson title: Your course workflow and campaign file
Objective: Set up the folder, naming system and AI workspace you will use for the whole course.
Demonstration: Screen recording: create the folder, paste the business profile prompt, save the first result
Assignment: Complete the business profile prompt from the Prompt Library and save the AI output in your campaign file.
Resources: Prompt Library (section A); Campaign Planning Worksheet
External needs: An AI assistant account of your choice (free tier is enough to start)

Lesson title: How the Meta ad auction and account structure work
Objective: Describe campaign, ad set and ad levels and what you control at each level.
Demonstration: Annotated diagram of a three level structure drawn from a hypothetical Lagos catering business
Assignment: Draw the campaign structure for your own offer with one campaign, two ad sets and three ads.
Resources: Structure diagram handout; Campaign Planning Worksheet

Lesson title: Placements, formats and how Nigerians use the platforms
Objective: Choose formats and placements that suit a mobile first Nigerian audience.
Demonstration: Screen recording: browse the Ads Manager placement options and the Meta Ad Library for local businesses
Assignment: List the three formats you will test first and write one sentence on why each suits your customer.
Resources: Campaign Planning Worksheet (Format selection section)
External needs: Meta Ad Library (free, no ad account needed)

Module title: Setting up Meta Business Suite and Ads Manager
Lesson title: Accounts you need: Page, Instagram, ad account and payment
Objective: Set up the assets required to run ads under your own control.
Demonstration: Screen recording on a fresh test setup, with personal details hidden
Assignment: Screenshot your ad account overview page (hide sensitive details) showing the account is active with a payment method added.
Resources: Campaign Launch Checklist (Accounts section)
External needs: A Facebook profile, a Page, an Instagram account, a payment method that Meta accepts for your account

Module title: Setting up Meta Business Suite and Ads Manager
Lesson title: Business verification, access and policy basics
Objective: Avoid account restrictions by understanding verification and advertising policy basics.
Demonstration: Screen recording: open the Advertising Standards page and the Account Quality page
Assignment: Read the current policy page for your category and write three things your ads must not say.
Resources: Campaign Launch Checklist (Policy section)

Lesson title: Choosing the right objective for your goal
Objective: Match a business goal to a campaign objective and a conversion event.
Demonstration: Screen recording: walk through the objective screen and the optimisation options for each
Assignment: Write your goal, your chosen objective, your conversion event and the destination, with one sentence of reasoning.
Resources: Campaign Planning Worksheet (Objective selection guide section)

Lesson title: Conversion tracking basics: what Meta needs to learn
Objective: Explain how conversion events let Meta find more of the people who act.
Demonstration: Slides plus a short screen recording of the Events Manager overview
Assignment: List which events your funnel should send, in order, from ad click to payment.
Resources: Tracking map (in Campaign Planning Worksheet)

Module title: Using AI for market and audience research
Lesson title: Writing a research brief AI can use
Objective: Give an AI assistant enough context to return useful research instead of generic text.
Demonstration: Screen recording: the same request with a weak prompt and with a full brief, compared side by side
Assignment: Run the research brief prompt for your business and mark each claim as verified, to verify, or discard.
Resources: Prompt Library (section B); Audience Research Worksheet

Module title: Using AI for market and audience research
Lesson title: Finding customer language: comments, reviews and competitor ads
Objective: Collect real customer wording from public sources to use in your hooks and copy.
Demonstration: Screen recording: search the Ad Library for a local category, then paste anonymous quotes into an AI assistant to cluster themes
Assignment: Collect 20 real customer phrases from public sources and cluster them into pains, desires and objections.
Resources: Audience Research Worksheet; Prompt Library (section B)
External needs: Meta Ad Library, a public source for your niche

Module title: Using AI for market and audience research
Lesson title: Turning research into audience hypotheses
Objective: Write three testable audience descriptions with the signals you would test in Ads Manager.
Demonstration: Screen recording: open Audiences in Ads Manager and build a saved audience from the worksheet
Assignment: Write three audience hypotheses and the Ads Manager settings that match each.
Resources: Audience Research Worksheet

Lesson title: Offer, desire and objection: building an angle map
Objective: Turn research into a map of angles you can test.
Demonstration: Worked example for a hypothetical Ibadan tailoring business, labelled as an invented teaching example
Assignment: Create an angle map with at least six angles for your offer.
Resources: Prompt Library (section C); Campaign Planning Worksheet

Lesson title: Scoring angles and choosing three to test
Objective: Choose three angles with a simple scoring method before spending anything.
Demonstration: Screen recording: score ten angles in the tracker sheet with AI help and rank them
Assignment: Submit your scoring table and the three angles you chose with one sentence each on why.
Resources: Performance Tracker (Angle scoring sheet); Prompt Library (section C)

Module title: Writing headlines, hooks and ad copy with AI
Lesson title: Hooks and headlines: generating many and choosing few
Objective: Generate 30 hooks for one angle and select the best five with clear criteria.
Demonstration: Screen recording: generate 30 hooks, strike out 25 with reasons, keep five
Assignment: Produce 30 hooks for your top angle and mark the best five with your reasons.
Resources: Ad Copy Templates; Prompt Library (section D)

Module title: Writing headlines, hooks and ad copy with AI
Lesson title: Full ad copy for three awareness levels
Objective: Write one ad for people who do not know the problem, know the problem, or know your solution.
Demonstration: Screen recording: draft three versions of the same ad, one per awareness level
Assignment: Write three full ads for your best angle, one per awareness level.
Resources: Ad Copy Templates; Prompt Library (section D)

Module title: Writing headlines, hooks and ad copy with AI
Lesson title: Editing AI copy: your voice, accuracy and policy
Objective: Turn an AI draft into copy that sounds like you, is true, and passes a policy check.
Demonstration: Screen recording: edit a raw draft line by line with a visible checklist
Assignment: Edit your three ads with the checklist and submit before and after versions.
Resources: Ad Copy Templates (edit checklist); Prompt Library (section D)

Lesson title: Creative briefs that get usable results
Objective: Write a creative brief that guides AI and any designer or editor you work with.
Demonstration: Screen recording: fill in the creative brief template for one ad
Assignment: Complete a creative brief for each of your three chosen angles.
Resources: Creative Brief Template

Lesson title: Static image ads with AI and design tools
Objective: Produce three static image ads in the correct sizes for Feed and Stories.
Demonstration: Screen recording: build one image ad in a design tool of your choice and export two sizes
Assignment: Create three static ads and submit the exported files with the brief each belongs to.
Resources: Creative Brief Template; Ad Copy Templates
External needs: A design tool and an AI image tool of your choice

Lesson title: Short video and UGC style ads: quality, disclosure and honesty
Objective: Plan and produce a short video ad that is honest about what it shows.
Demonstration: Screen recording of the edit, plus a phone recording setup demo
Assignment: Produce one short video ad under 30 seconds with captions and submit it with the script.
Resources: Creative Brief Template; Prompt Library (section E)
External needs: Phone camera, a video editor, AI script assistant

Lesson title: What the page must do after the click
Objective: Describe the parts of a landing page and match them to the promise in the ad.
Demonstration: Slides with before and after layout sketches, no invented results
Assignment: Sketch your landing page section by section and write the headline that matches your best ad.
Resources: Landing Page Section Guide (in Campaign Planning Worksheet)

Lesson title: Building a landing page with AI and a page builder
Objective: Build a mobile ready page with a working payment or lead button.
Demonstration: Screen recording: build a page section by section and add the button
Assignment: Publish your page and submit the link plus a screenshot of a successful test on a phone.
Resources: Landing Page Section Guide (in Campaign Planning Worksheet); Campaign Launch Checklist
External needs: A domain and hosting or a page builder account, a Paystack or lead form tool

Lesson title: WhatsApp as a destination: when it fits and how to manage it
Objective: Decide whether click to WhatsApp suits your offer and set up replies that convert.
Demonstration: Screen recording: set up the WhatsApp Business greeting and quick replies
Assignment: Write your first three WhatsApp replies and decide whether your funnel uses WhatsApp, a page, or both.
Resources: Ad Copy Templates (WhatsApp replies)

Module title: Setting up Meta Pixel and tracking
Lesson title: Creating and installing the Meta Pixel
Objective: Install the pixel on your page and confirm it loads.
Demonstration: Screen recording: install on a test page and fire PageView
Assignment: Submit a screenshot of your pixel receiving a PageView from your page.
Resources: Tracking map (in Campaign Planning Worksheet); Campaign Launch Checklist

Module title: Setting up Meta Pixel and tracking
Lesson title: Conversions API and event matching in plain language
Objective: Explain why server events help and what information you must handle carefully.
Demonstration: Slides and one screen recording of Events Manager diagnostics
Assignment: Decide whether you need server events now, and list who will set them up.
Resources: Tracking map (in Campaign Planning Worksheet)

Module title: Setting up Meta Pixel and tracking
Lesson title: Testing and debugging your tracking
Objective: Use the test tools to prove each event fires correctly before you spend.
Demonstration: Screen recording: go through the funnel and check every event in the Test Events view
Assignment: Submit your tracking test log showing each event, its value and pass or fail.
Resources: Campaign Launch Checklist (Tracking section)

Lesson title: Campaign structure and naming that make analysis easy
Objective: Plan a clean structure and naming system before you build.
Demonstration: Screen recording: generate a naming table and UTM links
Assignment: Create the naming table and UTM links for your campaign.
Resources: Prompt Library (section F); Campaign Planning Worksheet

Lesson title: Building your campaign in Ads Manager, step by step
Objective: Build a complete campaign from objective to ad without skipping a setting.
Demonstration: Screen recording of a full build using a hypothetical business, ending on the review screen without publishing
Assignment: Build your campaign in draft and submit screenshots of each level.
Resources: Campaign Launch Checklist

Lesson title: Using AI to speed up repetitive ad work
Objective: Automate the repetitive parts: variations, naming, notes and reports, while you keep control of spend.
Demonstration: Screen recording: export data and have AI draft a weekly review for you to check
Assignment: Create a reusable weekly report prompt and test it on sample data from the tracker.
Resources: Prompt Library (section G); Performance Tracker

Lesson title: Setting a budget from your own numbers
Objective: Work out what you can afford to learn and what one customer is worth to you.
Demonstration: Spreadsheet walk through with a hypothetical ₦14,999 product and invented costs
Assignment: Calculate your break even cost per customer and your test budget, and show your working.
Resources: Performance Tracker (Break even sheet)

Lesson title: Designing a clean test

Demonstration: Screen recording: set up a three ad test in Ads Manager and record it in the tracker
Assignment: Write your test plan: question, variable, ads, budget, duration and decision rule.
Resources: Performance Tracker (Test log sheet); Campaign Planning Worksheet

Lesson title: Decision rules: when to wait, change or stop
Objective: Use written rules so you do not react to noise.
Demonstration: Screen recording: apply decision rules to a sample data set
Assignment: Write five decision rules for your campaign and apply them to the sample data provided.
Resources: Campaign Optimisation Checklist; Performance Tracker

Lesson title: The metrics that matter and what they mean
Objective: Read the core metrics and connect each to a part of the funnel.
Demonstration: Slides plus an Ads Manager column walk through on a sample account view
Assignment: Build a custom column set and explain in one line what each column tells you.
Resources: Performance Tracker (Metric guide sheet)

Lesson title: Your tracker and weekly review with AI
Objective: Run a weekly review: export, enter, interpret and decide.
Demonstration: Screen recording: complete one weekly review on sample data
Assignment: Complete a weekly review on the sample data and submit your three decisions.
Resources: Performance Tracker; Prompt Library (section G)

Lesson title: The diagnostic tree: where is the problem?
Objective: Locate a problem as delivery, creative, click, page, offer or tracking.
Demonstration: Diagram walk through with five labelled hypothetical symptom sets
Assignment: Diagnose three symptom cases and name the first thing you would check for each.
Resources: Campaign Optimisation Checklist

Lesson title: Fixing problems: worked diagnostics
Objective: Apply the tree to sample data and write a fix list in order of priority.
Demonstration: Screen recording: diagnose two invented sample datasets supplied in the tracker
Assignment: Submit a diagnosis and fix plan for the two sample datasets.
Resources: Performance Tracker (Sample data sheet); Campaign Optimisation Checklist

Lesson title: Is this campaign ready to scale?
Objective: Decide with evidence whether scaling is justified.
Demonstration: Slides with a readiness checklist
Assignment: Complete the scaling readiness checklist for your campaign and state yes or not yet with reasons.
Resources: Campaign Optimisation Checklist (Scaling section)

Lesson title: Scaling methods and their risks
Objective: Choose a scaling method and set limits before you start.
Demonstration: Screen recording: duplicate an ad set and adjust budget in a draft
Assignment: Write your scaling plan with limits and a stop rule.
Resources: Campaign Optimisation Checklist; Performance Tracker

Lesson title: Account health, rejected ads and staying compliant
Objective: Respond correctly to rejections and protect your account.
Demonstration: Screen recording: open Account Quality and walk through the review options
Assignment: Write a response plan for a rejected ad and list the proof you keep for your claims.
Resources: Campaign Launch Checklist (Policy section)

Lesson title: Project brief and planning
Objective: Understand the project, grading criteria and what to submit at each stage.
Demonstration: Slides walking through the project brief and rubric
Assignment: Submit Stage 1: the complete Campaign Planning Worksheet for your campaign.
Resources: Campaign Project Brief and Rubric; Campaign Planning Worksheet

Lesson title: Launch review
Objective: Check your build against the launch checklist before publishing.
Demonstration: Screen recording: a launch review on a draft campaign
Assignment: Submit Stage 2: screenshots of every level and the completed launch checklist.
Resources: Campaign Launch Checklist

Lesson title: Running, reviewing and reporting
Objective: Review the first days of results and write an honest report with next actions.
Demonstration: Screen recording: write a results report from sample data
Assignment: Submit Stage 3: your seven day results report and next actions. If your budget does not allow a live run, submit a draft campaign with a full test plan.
